set.st: Hugo, Albert and Rudolph Donnerstag were arrested near Rhinelander in August 1908 for making counterfeit $5 gold pieces and silver; agents found $1,035 in spurious gold coin, plaster molds, lathes and a plating outfit, and 11 guns in the house. The mother tried to get away in a boat, so the home was on a lake; Hugo and Albert's place was about 18 miles out and Rudolph lived nearer the city. On Oct. 25 the three sawed a bar and went down a rope from the Dane County jail. They went straight home, and the Madison papers (Nov. 5) said it was because a pot of gold, $4,000 in gold coin, was secreted in the woods and they feared forest fires would destroy it. Hugo and Albert gave up at Rudolph's house about twelve miles from Rhinelander; Rudolph was shot in both legs while running through the woods near Manson Lake, eight miles west of the city, near the old Donnerstag home. None of the papers read says the $4,000 was dug up, and since they were coiners it may have been their own make. The local weekly places the family: in 1905 Rudolph Donnerstag 'of the town of Woodboro' was in court over a gun threat, and in September 1908 Hugo wrote from the Madison jail; he had earlier served time for killing his father. The Rhinelander weekly adds that the coining outfit and over a thousand dollars in bad money were found at 'their home in the woods near Manson', and that there were three dwellings: the Donnerstag place, Rudolph's own home some distance away, and the mother's house, which Rudolph reached by rowing across the lake; he was taken at a neighbour's house (Jones) and another neighbour (Serene) is named. Rudolph lost his left leg to the gunshot wound; the brothers were held in the Rock County jail at Janesville in December 1908. In 1909 the paper, describing the new Rhinelander-Tomahawk road, said 'a former four mile stretch beginning at the Donnerstag place' had been a dread to drivers, so the home place stood on that road. Pin is approximate (town or township only), not the spot itself.
pinev: Placed on Manson Lake (GNIS 45.5625, -89.6329) from 'near Manson lake, eight miles west' (Eagle River Review, Nov. 13, 1908); the house itself is not yet placed.
Rudolph Donnerstag was 'of the town of Woodboro' in 1905 (Rhinelander New North, 14 Sep 1905), which takes in Manson Lake; the land itself is not yet on a plat.
Three family dwellings around Manson Lake, one reached by boat across it, and neighbours Jones and Serene (Rhinelander New North, 5 Nov 1908): the parcels to look for on the Woodboro plat.
The Donnerstag place stood on the Rhinelander-Tomahawk road (Rhinelander New North, 7 Oct 1909), a plat anchor for the Woodboro search.
